title: Builds, deployment and rollback

objectives.text: Apply a bounded pure canary error-count gate with explicit eligible populations,minimum evidence and strict excess-error threshold without claiming significance or automatic deployment authority.
Check declared read/write schema rollback compatibility and explain immutable artifacts,staged rollout,migration/backup evidence and irreversible data limits.

blocks.markdown: A release binds reviewed source/build artifact digest,dependency/config/schema versions,migration plan,test evidence,environment,owner/authority,observation and rollback/restore. Build once and promote the same verified artifact rather than rebuilding unrecorded variations. A hash identifies bytes,not trusted build provenance or correctness. This lesson deploys nothing and purchases no service. A local gate can only evaluate supplied evidence,not grant authority or replace actual mobile/app/runtime/production tests.

GoogleSREdefines canarying as partial,time-limited deployment/evaluation against a control. Predefine population,traffic assignment,window,user-impact metrics,minimum evidence,stop/reset/escalation and observation duration. Unequal or contaminated traffic can bias comparisons;errors alone miss latency/data/security regressions. Low traffic or rare failures may require longer/more targeted tests,not automatic promotion because no error was seen.

blocks.caption: Expected stop-investigate;hold-insufficient-evidence;eligible-for-next-reviewed-step;False;True. Complete pure Fractioncounts/gate and declared read/write schema check. Strict excess>threshold;equal threshold passes only this descriptive rule. No CI/test significance,traffic routing,artifact authentication,migration,rollback/restore execution or full release approval.

blocks.markdown: A binary rollback does not reverse database writes or recover dropped columns. Google's release guidance describes a bridgeversion that tolerates the new schema before enabling new features. Expand/migrate/contract introduces new structure,backfills/verifies,changes compatible readers/writers,then removes old structure only after consumers have moved and recovery implications are understood. Dual-write consistency and new data not representable in old schema need explicit reconciliation;the pattern is not automatically zero downtime or fully reversible.

Preserve known-good artifact/configuration and verify it can read ANDwrite the current schema/data without corruption. Define traffic drain,queued requests,in-flight unknown outcomes,compatibility/feature flags and postrollback checks. Destructive/irreversible migrations may require forward fix or a tested restore with explicit data-loss/recovery-point consequences;do not blindly deploy an old binary. Restore authorization/data loss cannot be inferred from a generic request to make an app work.

Tests should bind actual artifact/revision/environment:unit/property/reference,contract/integration,migration/mixed-version,security/dependency,resource/performance,renderer/mobile/a11y/user flows and recovery. A source curriculum archive or green classroom gate is not deployed production evidence. Canary only after appropriate predeployment tests,with limited authorized exposure and monitoring;not a replacement for those tests. Stop on unexplained regressions and retain evidence instead of removing behavior to pass checks.

GoogleSRErelease/canary guidance describes practices and tradeoffs,not a universal recipe or approval for this user's accounts. Liquibasedescribes expand/migrate/contract;actual engine/transaction/locking/backfill behavior depends on database and migration tools. This own descriptive count gate and declared schema sets are deliberately narrow,no framework or platform is installed.

Independent transfer:enumerate small canary/control counts,compare exact rational differences and test empty/minimum/equality boundaries. Construct v1/bridge/v2read/write compatibility tables and reject read-only support when writes are needed. Design a schema-drop scenario where binary rollback is unsafe,and state forward-fix/restore choices with data-loss/authority gaps. Record outstanding actual app/production tests rather than invent a deployed success.

Sources:[GoogleSREcanarying](https://sre.google/workbook/canarying-releases/),[reliable releases/rollback and bridge schema](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/gcp/reliable-releases-and-rollbacks-cre-life-lessons),[Liquibaseexpand/contract](https://www.liquibase.com/technical-glossary/expand-contract-pattern),[incident mitigation context](https://sre.google/workbook/incident-response/). Own gate thresholds and compatibility records are synthetic,not current vendor policy or deployment commands.

summary: A release needs bound artifact/config/schema/evidence and authorized staged operations. A small error-only canary gate is descriptive evidence,not automatic approval. Binary rollback depends on current read/write data/schema compatibility and cannot undo irreversible migrations or restore lost data by itself.
